correctness.rationale: The short-step normal-residual formula is an exact algebraic identity. The Polyak expansion is obtained directly from f and its gradient, and composition yields x_next=(3/4)x+O(x^3). Two short steps reset the leading normal coefficient to 4/a; one short step gives the affine normal map with multiplier 8a/9. The local wedge is invariant after shrinking the neighborhood, so the asymptotic ratios follow.

value.rationale: The result identifies a sharp block-length mechanism on the motivating nonconvex benchmark: one curvature-matched short step has an exact parameter-dependent normal multiplier and threshold, while two short steps cancel the incoming normal mode and recover strict Q-linear convergence for all a>0. This explains a recent K=1 numerical observation, shows that the original a=10 benchmark needs no growing short-step block locally under curvature matching, and improves the model-specific oracle scale from the general O(log^2(1/epsilon)) guarantee to O(log(1/epsilon)).
